questions.question: The percentage profit made by selling an item for ₹ 1,800 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same item for ₹ 1,160. At what price should the item be sold to earn a profit of 20%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price at 20% profit = ₹1,800

Selling price at loss = ₹1,160

**Formula Used:**

Profit% = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Loss% = (Loss / Cost Price) x 100

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price be ₹C.

Profit when sold at ₹1,800 = Selling Price - Cost Price = ₹1,800 - ₹C

Loss when sold at ₹1,160 = Cost Price - Selling Price = ₹C - ₹1,160

Given, Profit% = Loss%

((1800 - C))/(C) times 100 = ((C - 1160))/(C) times 100 

⇒ 1,800 - C = C - 1,160

⇒ 1,800 + 1,160 = 2C

⇒ 2,960 = 2C

⇒ C = 1,480

Cost Price = ₹1,480

To find the selling price for 20% profit:

Profit = 20% of Cost Price

Profit = 0.20 x 1,480

Profit = ₹296

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

Selling Price = ₹1,480 + ₹296

Selling Price = ₹1,776

**The selling price for 20% profit is ₹1,776.**

questions.question: Ruby bought 20 buttons for Rs. 1. How many buttons she must sell for Rs. 1 in order to get a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a constant **Expenditure**, the **Quantity** is inversely proportional to the **Price**.

**Cost Price (CP)** percentage = 100% and **Selling Price (SP)** percentage for 25% profit = 125%.

Price Ratio (CP : SP) = 100 : 125 ⇒ 4 : 5.

Quantity Ratio (CP : SP) = 5 : 4.

Given 5 units = 20 buttons, then 1 unit = 4 buttons.

Selling Quantity = 4 units × 4 = 16 buttons.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 buttons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/059fe93fa11d4a47807a2700ef569566e6a27f27f5c17b4933c10ec053a9c060.png] 

**Given:**

Cost Price of 20 buttons = ₹1

Desired Profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 button = ₹1/20

⇒ SP of 1 button = (1/20) × (125/100)

⇒ SP of 1 button = (1/20) × (5/4)

⇒ SP of 1 button = ₹1/16

⇒ Number of buttons sold for ₹1 = 1 / (1/16) = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 buttons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price-Quantity Relationship

When the total expenditure remains constant, the **Quantity** is inversely proportional to the **Price**. If price increases by 25% (ratio 4:5), the quantity must decrease in the ratio 5:4.

Profit and Loss on Unitary Items

To find the gain or loss percent when cost and selling prices of different quantities are given, always equate the **Number of Articles** or use the price per **Single Unit**.

questions.question: A man buys 35 mangoes for a rupee. How many mangoes had he sold for a rupee so that there is a loss of 30 percent?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **Total Expenditure** is constant (₹1 in both cases), the **Quantity** is inversely proportional to the **Price**.

Price Ratio (CP : SP) = 100 : (100 − 30) = 100 : 70 = 10 : 7

Quantity Ratio (CP : SP) = 7 : 10

Given: CP quantity = 7 units → 35 mangoes

⇒ 1 unit = 5 mangoes

⇒ SP quantity = 10 units = 10 × 5 = 50 mangoes

**∴ The correct answer is 50 mangoes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of mangoes bought for ₹1 = 35

Loss percentage = 30%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/023edbb32421a5651db72beeb763df9b9eb6c627d289ba63be4d80a31e9aa876.png] 

**Formula:** Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100

⇒ **CP** of 35 mangoes = ₹1

⇒ **CP** of 1 mango = ₹1/35

⇒ **SP** of 1 mango = (1/35) × (100 − 30)/100

⇒ **SP** of 1 mango = (1/35) × (70/100)

⇒ **SP** of 1 mango = (1/35) × (7/10)

⇒ **SP** of 1 mango = 1/(5 × 10) = ₹1/50

⇒ Since **SP** of 1 mango is ₹1/50, the number of mangoes sold for ₹1 = 50

**∴ The correct answer is 50 mangoes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Price-Quantity Relationship

When expenditure is constant, Price per unit × Quantity = Constant. Thus, Price is inversely proportional to Quantity (P₁/P₂ = Q₂/Q₁).

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. All profit or loss percentages are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Direct SP Calculation

To find the selling price for a desired profit, use SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100. For loss, use SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100.

**Calculation:**

Repair cost = 9% of ₹7,200

⇒ Repair cost = 0.09 × 7200

⇒ Repair cost = ₹648

Total cost price = Cost price + Repair cost

⇒ Total cost price = ₹7,
200 + ₹648

Profit = Selling price - Total cost price

⇒ Profit = ₹8,100 - ₹7,848

⇒ Profit Percentage = 0.0321 × 100

questions.question: Two objects were sold for ₹9,900 each. One object was sold at a loss of 10% and the other object was sold at a gain of 10%. The net gain or loss in the whole transaction is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects are sold at the same SP with x% profit and x% loss, there is always a net loss of x² ÷ 100%.

Net Loss % = (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 1%.

Total SP = 9900 × 2 = ₹19,800, which is equivalent to 99% of Total CP (100% − 1%).

Loss amount = 1% of CP = (19800 ÷ 99) × 1 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SP of first object = ₹9,900, Profit = 10%

SP of second object = ₹9,900, Loss = 10%

**Formula Used:**

CP = [100 ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss %)] × SP

Loss = Total CP − Total SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87d00a006e3d8b25098bec35ef94f12c66097723edde5d4319ddc0641ff66838.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of first object = [100 ÷ (100 + 10)] × 9900

⇒ CP₁ = (100 ÷ 110) × 9900 = ₹9,000

⇒ CP of second object = [100 ÷ (100 − 10)] × 9900

⇒ CP₂ = (100 ÷ 90) × 9900 = ₹11,000

⇒ Total CP = 9000 + 11000 = ₹20,000

⇒ Total SP = 9900 + 9900 = ₹19,800

⇒ Net Loss = Total CP − Total SP

⇒ Net Loss = 20000 − 19800 = ₹200

**∴ The correct answer is Loss ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Selling Price Condition

When two items are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Cost Price Formula

CP can be directly calculated from SP using: CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 ± R)], where R is the profit or loss percentage.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: If 80 percent of total articles are sold at a profit of 25 percent and remaining articles are sold at a loss of 20 percent, then what will be the overall profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The 80% of total article sold at 25% profit

The remaining 20% sold at 20% loss

**Concept:**

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of items are X and cost price of each items be C

According to the question

The overall cost price = X × C = XC

The 80% items sold at 25% profit = (0.80 × X) × (1.25C) = XC

The remaining 20% items sold at 20% loss = (0.20 × X) × (0.80 × C) = 0.16XC

The total Selling price = XC + 0.16XC = 1.16XC

The profit percentage = {1.16XC-XCover XC}times 100={0.16 times 100}=16\%

**∴ The required result will be 16%.**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 160 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 160% of Cost Price (CP)

Discount = 20% of MP

Find Profit Percentage

**Concept:**

Profit or Loss is calculated on CP.

**Solution:**

Let the CP = 100 (For simplicity)

Hence, MP = 160 (As MP is 160% of CP)

Discount = 20% of MP = 20% of 160 = 32

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 160 - 32 = 128

Profit = SP - CP = 128 - 100 = 28

Profit Percentage = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (28/100) × 100 = 28%

**Hence, the profit percentage is 28% (Option 1).**

questions.question: 400 apples were bought at ₹1200 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹800. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of apples.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP for 400 apples = 4 × 1200 = ₹4800

Total SP = CP + Profit = 4800 + 800 = ₹5600

SP of 1 apple = 5600 ÷ 400 = ₹14

SP per dozen = 14 × 12 = ₹168

**∴ The correct answer is ₹168.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of apples = 400

Cost price per 100 apples = ₹1200

Total Profit = ₹800

**Formula Used:**

Total SP = Total CP + Profit

SP per dozen = SP of 1 unit × 12

 
 Total CP = ₹4800
 
 
 + Profit = ₹800
 
 
 Total SP = ₹5600 (for 400 apples)
 
 

 

 
 SP per dozen = (5600 ÷ 400) × 12 = ₹168

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost price of 100 apples = ₹1200

⇒ Total Cost price (CP) of 400 apples = 4 × 1200 = ₹4800

⇒ Total Selling price (SP) of 400 apples = Total CP + Profit

⇒ Total SP = 4800 + 800 = ₹5600

⇒ Selling price of 1 apple = 5600 ÷ 400 = ₹14

⇒ Selling price per dozen (12 apples) = 14 × 12 = ₹168

**∴ The correct answer is ₹168.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the selling price is greater than the cost price (Profit = SP − CP). Loss occurs when the cost price is greater than the selling price (Loss = CP − SP).

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the base cost price. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method Application

The unitary method helps in finding the value of a single unit from the value of a multiple unit, which is then used to find the value of any required number of units. Here it was used to find the SP of a dozen (12 units) items.
